channel.title: Identity Field Notes
channel.description: AI-driven, source-linked identity security news for practitioners.

item.title: A Quiet Morning, Except for One Stolen Police Login
item.description: The strongest new identity-relevant disclosure is a Florida DMV breach tied to credentials improperly stored on an employee’s personal device; no comparable new PAM, IGA, passkey, or agent-authorization development cleared the bar without recycling recently covered news.

item.title: When the Workflow Is the Identity Boundary
item.description: The strongest new signals are not another MFA feature, but evidence that AI workflows and stolen machine credentials are becoming direct authorization paths into enterprise data.

item.title: The identity control plane is getting crowded
item.description: Okta pushes deeper into PAM and IGA, agent administration moves into the IAM control plane, and active cloud intrusions show why MFA alone is not a session-security strategy.

item.title: The service account problem is becoming the agent identity problem
item.description: AI agents are adding speed and autonomy to an identity class most organizations already struggle to inventory and govern.

item.title: Privilege is moving from account-level to action-level
item.description: AI agents are forcing PAM teams to ask a harder question than who got access: what was the identity allowed to do after the session opened?

item.title: Authentication succeeded. That does not mean the session is trustworthy.
item.description: Recent research makes the case for treating session tokens, MFA seed material and post-authentication persistence as privileged assets in their own right.
